title: A closed normal subgroup is a representation kernel
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $G$ be an affine group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme, def-pc-scheme] of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $N\subseteq G$ be a closed normal subgroup scheme [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. There exist an integer $r\geq1$ and a homomorphism of group schemes $\rho:G\to\mathrm{GL}_{r,k}$ [def-sc-general-linear-group] whose scheme-theoretic kernel is $N$. Explicitly, for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$, one has $N(A)=\{g\in G(A):\rho_A(g)=I_r\}$, naturally in $A$. No smoothness, reducedness, connectedness, perfectness or characteristic hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Corollary 5.19, printed p.103; its input Lemma 5.17 and the restriction-of-scalars construction in the proof of Proposition 5.18, printed pp.102--103. A trivial summand permits r >= 1.

proof.text: First work over an algebraically closed field $K$. Apply [lem-sfb-normal-subgroup-character-inversion] to the closed normal subgroup $N_K\subseteq G_K$. It supplies exactly the occurrence hypothesis of [lem-sfb-chevalley-character-cancellation]. Thus choose a rational $G_K$-representation $V$ and a line $L\subseteq V$, fixed pointwise by $N_K$, with $N_K(A)=\{g:gL_A=L_A\}$ for every $K$-algebra $A$. All occurrences and stabilizers here are scheme-theoretic, not just assertions on $K$-points.

Put $U=V^{N_K}$. By [lem-sfb-rational-fixed-space-base-change], $U$ is a rational $G_K$-subrepresentation, $U_A$ is the full functorial fixed submodule, and $N_K$ acts trivially on it. Since $N_K$ fixes $L$ pointwise, $L\subseteq U$. If $g\in G_K(A)$ acts identically on $U_A$, it fixes $L_A$, hence belongs to its stabilizer $N_K(A)$ by step 1. Conversely every $n\in N_K(A)$ acts identically on $U_A$. Thus the restricted representation has kernel $N_K$ on all algebras. The line makes $U\ne0$; choosing a basis yields $\alpha_K:G_K\to\mathrm{GL}_{n,K}$ with $n\geq1$.

source.place: Lemma 5.17, second and third sentences; Lemma 5.15 and Proposition 4.31.

proof.text: Return to arbitrary $k$ and choose an algebraic closure $K$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. The finite intermediate fields $L\subseteq K$ are directed: the field generated by two finite lists of algebraic elements is finite and contains both fields. Their union is $K$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-colimit-limit], $\operatorname{Spec}K=\varprojlim_L\operatorname{Spec}L$. The bases are affine, hence qcqs, with affine transition maps. The schemes $G$, $G\times_kG$, and $\mathrm{GL}_{n,k}$ are of finite presentation: [lem-pc-affine-finite-type-algebra] gives finite-type coordinate algebras, fields are Noetherian (their only ideals are $0,k$), and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation] applies; products use the finite tensor presentation [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. Apply clause (2) of [thm-pd-spreading-out] to descend $\alpha_K$ to a morphism $\alpha_L:G_L\to\mathrm{GL}_{n,L}$ for some finite $L/k$.

source.place: Proposition 5.18, first sentence, making finite descent explicit; Stacks Tag 01ZM (limits.tex, lemma-descend-finite-presentation), clause (2).

proof.text: Apply clause (3) of [thm-pd-spreading-out] to $\alpha_L\circ m_G$ and $m_{\mathrm{GL}}\circ(\alpha_L\times\alpha_L)$, and to $\alpha_L\circ e_G$ and $e_{\mathrm{GL}}$. They agree after extension to $K$, so, after enlarging the finite field $L$ once, both identities hold over $L$. Thus $\alpha_L$ is a group homomorphism (inverses follow by applying the multiplication identity to $g,g^{-1}$). Its kernel is $N_L$: the two closed subschemes have equal defining ideals after tensoring with $K$, by step 2. Tensoring an $L$-vector space with $K$ is injective on the map $v\mapsto v\otimes1$ (extend a nonzero vector to a basis), so equality of the extended ideals implies equality before extension, by applying this to each quotient by one ideal. This also shows that no separability assumption is needed.

source.place: Proposition 5.18, finite-extension choice; Stacks Tag 01ZM (limits.tex, lemma-descend-finite-presentation), clause (3), and faithful field scalar extension.

proof.text: Choose a $k$-basis $b_1,\ldots,b_d$ of $L$. For a $k$-algebra $A$, send $g\in G(A)$ first to $g_L\in G_L(L\otimes_kA)$ and then let $\alpha_L(g_L)$ act on $(L\otimes_kA)^n$, viewed as the free $A$-module with basis $b_s e_i$. This defines a natural homomorphism $\beta_A:G(A)\to\mathrm{GL}_{nd}(A)$. It is a scheme morphism explicitly: write each matrix coefficient of $\alpha_L$ in $L\otimes_k k[G]$ in the basis $b_s$; multiplication by each $b_s$ has a fixed $d\times d$ matrix over $k$, so replacing each entry by its multiplication matrix gives an $nd\times nd$ matrix over $k[G]$. The inverse matrix is obtained from $\alpha_L^{-1}$ by the same substitution. Hence [def-sc-general-linear-group] supplies the homomorphism $\beta:G\to\mathrm{GL}_{nd,k}$. All formulas commute with $A\to A'$.

source.place: Proposition 5.18, restriction-of-scalars formula on R-points; Section 2.56, here written as multiplication matrices.

proof.text: For every $A$, the operator in step 5 is the identity if and only if the original $n\times n$ matrix over $L\otimes_kA$ is the identity: apply it to the standard vectors $e_i$. By step 4 this is equivalent to $g_L\in N_L(L\otimes_kA)$. Write $N$ as the closed subscheme cut out by an ideal $J\subseteq k[G]$. Membership of $g_L$ says that every $g^*(f)$, $f\in J$, vanishes in $L\otimes_kA$. The map $A\to L\otimes_kA$ is injective: a $k$-linear functional $t:L\to k$ with $t(1)=1$ gives the left inverse $t\otimes1$. Thus precisely $g\in N(A)$. Consequently $\ker\beta=N$ naturally on all algebras, hence scheme-theoretically. Since $n,d\geq1$, $r=nd\geq1$, completing every clause without smoothness, reducedness or characteristic assumptions.

lean.statement: theorem normal_subgroup_representation_kernel {k : Type u} [Field k] (G N : Over (Spec (.of k))) [GrpObj G] [GrpObj N] [IsAffine G.left] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom] [QuasiCompact G.hom] (i : N ⟶ G) [IsClosedSubgroupScheme i] [IsNormalSubgroupScheme i] : ∃ (r : ℕ), 1 ≤ r ∧ ∃ (ρ : G ⟶ GeneralLinearGroup (LinearGroupSchemes.Index.{u} r) k) (_ : IsMonHom ρ), (∃ e : N ≅ GrpObj.ker ρ, e.hom ≫ GrpObj.kerι ρ = i) ∧ ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] (g : (Spec (.of A)).asOver (Spec (.of k)) ⟶ G), (∃ h : (Spec (.of A)).asOver (Spec (.of k)) ⟶ N, h ≫ i = g) ↔ GeneralLinearGroup.homMulEquiv (LinearGroupSchemes.Index.{u} r) k A (g ≫ ρ) = 1
